q: Non-metals are the chemical elements that mostly lack the characteristics of ____.
e: Non-metals generally lack metallic properties such as high electrical conductivity, malleability, and luster.

q: Non-metals are located on the ____ of the Periodic Table.
e: Non-metals occupy the upper right portion of the periodic table, excluding hydrogen.

q: Among non-metals, ____ non-metals are solids, and 11 non-metals are gases.
e: There are 6 solid non-metals (e.g., carbon, sulphur, phosphorus) and 11 gaseous non-metals.

q: Only one non-metal, ____, is a liquid.
e: Bromine is the only non-metallic element that exists as a liquid at room temperature.

q: Nitrogen is the non-metallic element with the symbol ____ and atomic number 7.
e: Nitrogen is represented by the chemical symbol N and has an atomic number of 7.

q: A nitrogen molecule has two nitrogen atoms joined together by ____.
e: The strong triple covalent bond in $N_2$ makes nitrogen gas very unreactive.

q: Nitrogen is a ____ without any smell and is very unreactive.
e: Nitrogen gas is colourless, odourless, and chemically inert under normal conditions.

q: Nitrogen has a very low boiling point of ____.
e: Due to weak intermolecular forces, nitrogen boils at a very low temperature of -196℃.

q: The Earth's atmosphere is made up of ____ of nitrogen, with the rest being oxygen, carbon dioxide and other trace elements.
e: Nitrogen is the most abundant gas in the Earth's atmosphere, making up about 78% by volume.

q: Industrially, elemental nitrogen can be manufactured by ____ from which carbon dioxide and water have been removed.
e: Fractional distillation separates nitrogen from other components of liquefied air based on boiling points.

q: Air from this bottle is displaced and made to pass through another bottle B containing ____ to remove carbon dioxide.
e: Caustic soda (sodium hydroxide) reacts with and removes carbon dioxide from the air.

q: The carbon dioxide free air is then passed over ____ which absorbs oxygen to form copper(II) oxide.
e: Heated copper reacts with oxygen in the air to form copper(II) oxide, leaving nitrogen behind.

q: Since the nitrogen is only slightly soluble in water, it is collected by the ____.
e: Nitrogen's low solubility in water allows it to be collected over water.

q: The main use of nitrogen is in the manufacture of ____, from which nitrogenous fertilisers, nitric acid and urea are mainly prepared.
e: Ammonia is the primary intermediate chemical produced from nitrogen for fertilisers and acids.

q: Since nitrogen has ____ in its outermost shell, the oxidation numbers of nitrogen vary from -3 to +5.
e: With 5 valence electrons, nitrogen can gain 3 or lose up to 5 electrons, leading to varied oxidation states.

q: Some common oxides of nitrogen are ____, nitrogen oxide and nitrogen dioxide.
e: Dinitrogen oxide ($N_2O$), nitrogen oxide ($NO$), and nitrogen dioxide ($NO_2$) are common nitrogen oxides.

q: Dinitrogen oxide is readily decomposed above ____.
e: At temperatures above 600℃, dinitrogen oxide decomposes into nitrogen and oxygen gases.

q: At ____, nitrogen dioxide exists as a solid, colourless dimer molecule, dinitrogen tetroxide, $N_2O_4$.
e: Nitrogen dioxide dimerises to form colourless dinitrogen tetroxide at low temperatures like -10℃.

q: Dinitrogen oxide supports combustion as actively as ____ and it produces nitrogen when heated.
e: Dinitrogen oxide decomposes to release oxygen, allowing it to support combustion similarly to pure oxygen.

q: Nitrogen dioxide, an acidic oxide, dissolves in water to form a mixture of ____ and nitrous acid.
e: Nitrogen dioxide reacts with water to produce a mixture of nitric acid ($HNO_3$) and nitrous acid ($HNO_2$).

q: Dinitrogen oxide gas (laughing gas) is used as ____ for minor surgical operations.
e: Dinitrogen oxide has mild anaesthetic and analgesic properties, making it useful in minor surgeries.

q: The most thermally stable hydride of nitrogen is ____.
e: Ammonia ($NH_3$) is the most stable binary compound formed by nitrogen and hydrogen.

q: In the Haber process, nitrogen and hydrogen gases are mixed together in the ratio of ____ by volume.
e: The stoichiometric ratio for the Haber process is 1 volume of nitrogen to 3 volumes of hydrogen.

q: The mixture is passed over an ____ at a high pressure of about 200 atm and a moderately high temperature of 450℃.
e: An iron catalyst is used in the Haber process to speed up the synthesis of ammonia.

q: An excess of the ____, $Ca(OH)_2$ and ammonium chloride are mixed.
e: Slaked lime (calcium hydroxide) is reacted with ammonium chloride to prepare ammonia gas in the laboratory.

q: It is dried by passage through a lime tower which contains the drying agent, ____, $CaO$.
e: Quicklime (calcium oxide) is used to dry ammonia gas because it does not react with it.

q: Since ammonia is lighter than air and very soluble in water, it is collected by the ____.
e: Ammonia's low density compared to air makes downward displacement of air the suitable collection method.

q: Ammonia gas should not be dried by usual drying agents such as ____, concentrated sulphuric acid and phosphorus(V) oxide.
e: Ammonia reacts with these drying agents to form addition compounds, so they cannot be used.

q: Ammonia is a colourless gas with a characteristic ____.
e: Ammonia is easily identifiable by its sharp, pungent odour.

q: Liquid ammonia boils at ____ and freezes at -77.7℃.
e: Ammonia has a relatively high boiling point for a gas of its size due to hydrogen bonding.

q: Dense ____ are observed when ammonia gas reacts with hydrogen chloride gas to form solid ammonium chloride.
e: The reaction between ammonia and hydrogen chloride gases produces a visible cloud of solid ammonium chloride.

q: When ammonia is passed over heated copper(II) oxide, it reduces the copper(II) oxide to ____.
e: Ammonia acts as a reducing agent, reducing copper(II) oxide to metallic copper.

q: When excess ammonia reacts with chlorine, ____ is obtained.
e: Excess ammonia reduces chlorine, resulting in the liberation of nitrogen gas and ammonium chloride.

q: If the chlorine is in excess, the explosive oily liquid substance, ____ is formed.
e: Excess chlorine reacts with ammonia to form highly explosive nitrogen trichloride ($NCl_3$).

q: Thus, dry ammonia passed over sodium metal heated to red heat forms ____ (sodamide).
e: Sodium reacts with dry ammonia at high temperatures to produce sodium amide ($NaNH_2$) and hydrogen.

q: However, magnesium forms the ____.
e: When heated in ammonia, magnesium reacts to form magnesium nitride ($Mg_3N_2$).

q: Nitric acid ($HNO_3$), known as ____ (Latin for "strong water"), is a more common and highly corrosive mineral acid.
e: Aqua fortis is the historical name for nitric acid, reflecting its strong corrosive nature.

q: Nitric acid is manufactured by the ____.
e: The Ammonia Oxidation Process (Ostwald process) is the industrial method for producing nitric acid.

q: The nitrogen oxide so formed is rapidly cooled and made to combine with oxygen from excess of air to form nitrogen dioxide, a ____.
e: Nitrogen dioxide ($NO_2$) is characterised by its distinct reddish-brown colour.

q: If nitric acid is subject to ____, decomposition occurs.
e: Nitric acid is unstable and decomposes into nitrogen dioxide, oxygen, and water when exposed to heat or light.

q: For this reason, it should be stored in ____.
e: Brown glass bottles protect nitric acid from light, preventing its decomposition.

q: Nitric acid is a colourless, ____.
e: Concentrated nitric acid releases fumes of nitrogen dioxide in moist air.

q: Dilute nitric acid neutralises bases, forming ____.
e: Like other acids, dilute nitric acid reacts with bases in a neutralisation reaction to produce nitrate salts and water.

q: Nitric acid oxidises metals to give ____.
e: Due to its strong oxidising property, nitric acid converts most metals into their corresponding nitrate salts.

q: With the reactive metal such as magnesium and dilute nitric acid, ____ is liberated.
e: Very reactive metals like magnesium can displace hydrogen from very dilute nitric acid.

q: With a less reactive metal such as zinc or aluminium and hot dilute nitric acid, ____ is produced.
e: Dilute nitric acid acting on less reactive metals like zinc can be reduced all the way to ammonium nitrate.

q: The ability of aqua regia (____ and 1 volume concentrated $HNO_3$) to dissolve the noble metal gold is due to the oxidation of the hydrochloric acid by the nitric acid.
e: Aqua regia is a 3:1 mixture of concentrated hydrochloric acid and concentrated nitric acid.

q: Nitric acid is used in the manufacture of ____, the production of ammonium nitrate fertiliser, and the preparation of aqua regia.
e: Nitric acid is a key raw material in synthesising various explosives (like TNT) and synthetic dyes.

q: Sulphur is the non-metallic solid element with the symbol S and atomic number ____.
e: Sulphur is located in Group 16 of the periodic table with an atomic number of 16.

q: Sulphur is a ____, strong smelling solid element.
e: Elemental sulphur is characteristically a bright yellow solid at room temperature.

q: Nowadays most sulphur is obtained from the sulphur compounds found in ____.
e: The majority of commercial sulphur is recovered as a byproduct from petroleum and natural gas processing.

q: It is also widely found in nature as ____ (iron sulphide), galena (lead(II) sulphide), gypsum (calcium sulphate), epsom salts (magnesium sulphate) and many other minerals.
e: Iron pyrites ($FeS_2$) is one of the most common sulphur-containing minerals in the Earth's crust.

q: The structural unit in the solid state of sulphur is the ____.
e: Solid sulphur primarily consists of crown-shaped $S_8$ ring molecules.

q: There are three allotropes of sulphur. Two of which are crystalline forms (rhombic and monoclinic) and the third is ____.
e: Plastic sulphur is the amorphous, non-crystalline allotrope of sulphur.

q: When a solution of sulphur in ____ is allowed to evaporate slowly at room temperature, the octahedral crystals of rhombic sulphur are deposited from the solution.
e: Carbon disulphide is a good solvent for sulphur, and slow evaporation yields rhombic crystals.

q: Monoclinic (or prismatic) sulphur slowly changes into the rhombic form at temperatures below ____ (369K) which is the transition temperature.
e: 96℃ is the transition temperature where monoclinic sulphur becomes thermodynamically unstable and converts to rhombic sulphur.

q: When any form of sulphur is heated almost to its boiling point and then poured into ____, plastic sulphur is formed.
e: Rapid cooling of molten sulphur in cold water prevents crystal formation, resulting in amorphous plastic sulphur.

q: In the plastic sulphur, the $S_8$ ring molecules are ruptured and the sulphur atoms join together to form long chains with a ____.
e: The polymeric chains in plastic sulphur are arranged in a zig-zag pattern, giving it a rubbery texture.

q: Sulphur, which is deposited at about ____ below the Earth's surface, is mined or extracted by the Frasch Process.
e: The Frasch Process is specifically designed to extract sulphur from deep underground deposits (around 700 ft).

q: Superheated steam at about ____ is forced down under pressure through the outermost pipe.
e: Superheated steam at 160℃ is used to melt the underground sulphur deposits.

q: Hot air under high pressure is forced down through the ____.
e: Compressed hot air forces the molten sulphur up through the middle pipe to the surface.

q: Sulphur obtained by this process is ____ pure.
e: The Frasch Process yields highly pure sulphur, typically 99.5% pure, as it is melted and separated underground.

q: Sulphur has two important oxides: sulphur dioxide, $SO_2$ and ____.
e: Sulphur dioxide ($SO_2$) and sulphur trioxide ($SO_3$) are the two primary oxides of sulphur.

q: Sulphur dioxide combines with oxygen in the presence of catalyst such as ____ or vanadium(V) oxide at the appropriate temperature.
e: Platinum or vanadium(V) oxide acts as a catalyst in the oxidation of sulphur dioxide to sulphur trioxide.

q: Sulphur dioxide directly combines with chlorine in the presence of ____ to form sulphuryl chloride.
e: Sunlight provides the activation energy for the direct combination of sulphur dioxide and chlorine.

q: Sulphur dioxide reacts with basic oxide to form ____.
e: As an acidic oxide, sulphur dioxide reacts with basic metal oxides to form sulphite salts.

q: Sulphur dioxide reduces halogens to ____.
e: In the presence of water, sulphur dioxide acts as a reducing agent, converting halogens to their corresponding hydrogen halides.

q: Sulphur dioxide can also reduce ____ acidified potassium permanganate solution to colourless solution.
e: The reduction of the violet permanganate ion ($MnO_4^-$) to the colourless manganese(II) ion ($Mn^{2+}$) is a test for $SO_2$.

q: Sulphur dioxide can also reduce orange coloured acidified potassium dichromate solution to a ____.
e: Sulphur dioxide reduces the orange dichromate ion ($Cr_2O_7^{2-}$) to the green chromium(III) ion ($Cr^{3+}$).

q: Sulphur dioxide bleaches colouring matter by ____.
e: Unlike chlorine which bleaches by oxidation, sulphur dioxide bleaches by reduction in the presence of moisture.

q: The bleaching action of sulphur dioxide is due to the reducing property of ____.
e: Sulphur dioxide reacts with water to produce nascent hydrogen, which is the actual reducing agent responsible for bleaching.

q: Sulphur dioxide can oxidise ____ and carbon monoxide.
e: Although primarily a reducing agent, $SO_2$ can act as an oxidising agent towards strong reducing agents like magnesium.

q: Sulphur dioxide is used in the food industries, as a ____.
e: Sulphur dioxide inhibits the growth of bacteria and fungi, making it an effective food preservative.

q: Sulphur dioxide acts as a ____.
e: It is commonly used to bleach delicate materials like wool, silk, and straw that would be damaged by chlorine.

q: Sulphur dioxide is a primary source material for manufacturing ____.
e: The oxidation of sulphur dioxide to sulphur trioxide is the crucial step in the Contact Process for making sulphuric acid.

q: In the laboratory, hydrogen sulphide gas is prepared by the action of ____ on metal sulphides.
e: Dilute, non-oxidising acids like HCl or $H_2SO_4$ are used to prevent the oxidation of the produced $H_2S$.

q: The gas evolved is soluble in water and heavier than air, so it is collected by the ____.
e: Due to its higher density compared to air, hydrogen sulphide is collected by upward displacement of air.

q: When a piece of paper soaked with ____ is placed near the mouth of the gas jar, the paper turns black if the gas jar is full with hydrogen sulphide.
e: Hydrogen sulphide reacts with lead(II) nitrate to form black lead(II) sulphide, serving as a positive test.

q: Hydrogen sulphide is a colourless gas with ____.
e: The distinct, foul odour of rotten eggs is the most recognizable physical property of hydrogen sulphide.

q: Hydrogen sulphide is slightly acidic (turns ____) and very poisonous.
e: As a weak acid, hydrogen sulphide turns moist blue litmus paper red or pink.

q: In a limited supply of oxygen, hydrogen sulphide burns to produce ____.
e: Incomplete combustion of $H_2S$ yields water and solid sulphur.

q: In an excess of oxygen, hydrogen sulphide burns to produce ____.
e: Complete combustion of $H_2S$ in plenty of oxygen produces water and sulphur dioxide gas.

q: Hydrogen sulphide reacts with all metals in the reactivity series except ____.
e: Gold and platinum are noble metals and do not react with hydrogen sulphide.

q: Hydrogen sulphide reduces ____.
e: Hydrogen sulphide is a strong reducing agent and readily reduces halogens to hydrogen halides.

q: Hydrogen sulphide reduces acidified potassium permanganate solution (____) to a colourless solution.
e: The violet permanganate is reduced to colourless manganese(II) ions by hydrogen sulphide.

q: Hydrogen sulphide reduces acidified potassium dichromate solution (orange colour) to a ____.
e: The orange dichromate is reduced to green chromium(III) ions, and sulphur is precipitated.

q: The best known and most important industrially use of sulphur oxoacid is ____.
e: Sulphuric acid ($H_2SO_4$) is the most significant and widely produced sulphur oxoacid in industry.

q: Sulphuric acid is manufactured by the ____.
e: The Contact Process is the modern industrial method for producing high-concentration sulphuric acid.

q: In this process, sulphur or ____ is burnt in excess air to produce sulphur dioxide.
e: Iron pyrites ($FeS_2$) or elemental sulphur is roasted in air to generate the required sulphur dioxide.

q: The gas mixture, $SO_2$ and excess air, contains impurities (especially ____).
e: Arsenious oxide is a common impurity that must be removed because it poisons the catalyst.

q: It is passed into a ____ to remove impurities which might poison the catalyst.
e: The wash tower cleans the gas mixture to protect the expensive catalyst from deactivation.

q: The mixture of sulphur dioxide and excess air is passed into the drying tower and dried by spraying with ____.
e: Concentrated sulphuric acid is an excellent drying agent that removes moisture without reacting with $SO_2$.

q: The dried sulphur dioxide and excess air are passed over platinum or vanadium(V) oxide catalyst at ____ to produce sulphur trioxide.
e: This temperature range provides the optimal compromise between reaction rate and equilibrium yield for $SO_3$ production.

q: Sulphur trioxide is easily dissolved in the concentrated sulphuric acid to form a product called ____, $H_2S_2O_7$.
e: Oleum (fuming sulphuric acid) is formed because $SO_3$ dissolves readily in concentrated $H_2SO_4$.

q: The oleum is then diluted with ____ to produce the acid of any desired concentration.
e: Controlled addition of water to oleum safely produces concentrated sulphuric acid without violent splattering.

q: Sulphuric acid is a ____, oily and heavy liquid.
e: Pure sulphuric acid is a colourless, viscous, and dense liquid.

q: The density of sulphuric acid is ____.
e: Sulphuric acid is significantly denser than water, with a density of 1.84 g mL$^{-1}$.

q: Sulphuric acid boils at about ____.
e: The high boiling point is due to extensive hydrogen bonding between sulphuric acid molecules.

q: Dilute sulphuric acid reacts with iron and the metals above iron in the reactivity series producing ____.
e: Like typical dilute acids, it displaces hydrogen from metals above it in the reactivity series, forming sulphate salts.

q: Concentrated sulphuric acid is a very powerful ____.
e: It has a strong affinity for water and can remove water molecules from many compounds.

q: Blue copper(II) sulphate becomes ____ when it is mixed with concentrated sulphuric acid.
e: Concentrated sulphuric acid removes the water of crystallisation from blue hydrated copper(II) sulphate, leaving white anhydrous copper(II) sulphate.

q: Sugar, starch and other carbohydrates are dehydrated by concentrated sulphuric acid. ____ is formed as the final product.
e: Concentrated sulphuric acid strips hydrogen and oxygen (as water) from carbohydrates, leaving behind a black mass of carbon.

q: Hence, when concentrated sulphuric acid is added to these compounds, they turn ____.
e: The formation of elemental carbon causes the characteristic blackening or charring effect.

q: Hot concentrated sulphuric acid oxidises ____.
e: When hot and concentrated, sulphuric acid acts as a strong oxidising agent, reacting with both metals and non-metals.

q: Copper reacts with concentrated sulphuric acid to produce ____.
e: Copper is oxidised to copper(II) sulphate, while the sulphuric acid is reduced to sulphur dioxide gas.

q: Carbon is oxidised to ____ when it reacts with hot concentrated sulphuric acid.
e: Hot concentrated sulphuric acid oxidises elemental carbon to carbon dioxide gas.

q: The major use of sulphuric acid is in the production of ____, e.g., superphosphate and ammonium sulphate.
e: The largest global consumption of sulphuric acid is in the agricultural sector for manufacturing phosphate and nitrogen fertilisers.

q: Sulphuric acid is widely used in the manufacture of chemicals e.g., ____, nitric acid, sulphate salts, synthetic detergents, dyes and pigments, explosives and drugs.
e: Sulphuric acid is a foundational chemical used to produce many other important industrial acids and compounds.

q: Dilute sulphuric acid is used in ____.
e: Dilute sulphuric acid serves as the electrolyte in automotive lead-acid batteries.
